# State of the seabed - North Sea

## Introduction

The area of interest covers a broad part of the southern and central North Sea, extending offshore from the east coast of England and across waters adjacent to the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany. The delineated area includes the Hollandse Kust West Wind Farm Zone off the Dutch coast, which has been the subject of Deltares morphodynamic assessments. The location and extent of the area of interest are shown in Figure 1.

## Reports

Previous Deltares work in the Dutch sector of the North Sea has considered seabed geology, morphology, and hydrodynamics, including an initial assessment of the Hollandse Kust West Wind Farm Zone (White, 2023). More recent work on Hollandse Kust West used available bathymetric data to assess seabed morphodynamics and to update the understanding of seabed-level development (Deltares, 2025).

The reported morphodynamic assessment approach distinguishes and evaluates bedforms, including sand waves and megaripples. These features are relevant because their migration and reshaping can affect local seabed levels. The Hollandse Kust West update includes analyses of sand-wave migration rates and directions, historic bed-level trends, and scenarios for future seabed levels (Deltares, 2025). The study also identifies uncertainty associated with bathymetric-data collection, grid resolution, sand-wave reshaping, megaripple dimensions, and vertical seabed-level trends.

For North Sea sites where mobile bedforms occur, seabed characterization therefore requires consideration of the presence and movement of sand waves, megaripples, and sand banks, together with observed bathymetric change. Such analysis supports the identification of areas where seabed mobility may influence future seabed levels (Deltares, 2025).
